titre: The Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Is an Event Even if You’re Not Playing It
chapo: Watching personal reactions to Nintendo's Switch 2 version of The Legend of Zelda: OoT is beautiful
extrait: Watching people's personal responses to this classic is beautiful As I mentioned last week, I'm not playing the Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time yet. I'm familiar enough with the game not to be too wary of spoilers, though, so I've been reading around it and watching the responses flood my feeds. It's been a beautiful and uplifting experience. Even from this distance, it's clearly the gaming event of the year (until next week, anyway). Everyone's enjoying themselves. The care and joy Nintendo's Zelda team poured into this remake is infectious, and the mood is celebratory. No tedious discourse has penetrated my feeds, and everyone's initial misgivings about the art style do not seem to have survived first contact with the game itself. Wild new caricatures of familiar characters delight me as I scroll past them. What's even more delightful is to see how directly and profoundly Ocarina of Time still connects with people, whether they're revisiting it, experiencing it for the first time, or just being reminded of it because it's in the aether. Polygon's Corey Plante wrote a deeply touching story about his memories playing Ocarina with his grandmother this week; at the other end of the scale, Jen Glennon shared her experience of playing the game for the first time as only a recent Zelda convert. It turns out the familiar, emotive connection everyone is feeling with the remake isn't just nostalgia. "It shouldn't be possible to feel nostalgic for a memory that isn't yours," Jen wrote. In Zelda, "you know exactly where you are, even if you've technically never been there before." Jen points out that this feeling of knowing the game even if it's new to you stems from the elemental, fairytale simplicity of the storytelling in Zelda games. I'd add that Zelda games share a deep humanity, too, more so than most Nintendo games, which tend to be quite abstract. In Zelda, this isn't expressed through strong emotions and high drama so much as it is through humor, caricature, pathos, and telling details. And no Zelda game is more poignant, funny, or scary than Ocarina of Time — not even the complex clockwork soap opera of its sequel, Majora's Mask. One thing that brought me up short this week was the revelation — by no means new, but new to me, and many others — that Ocarina of Time contains a sly reference to Louisa May Alcott's classic novel Little Women. titre: Excursion du Fossoyeur Zelda Ocarina of Time : Où trouver ce quart de coeur du cimetière ?
chapo: Découvrez comment récupérer le quart de coeur enfoui dans le cimetière du remake Switch 2 de Zelda OOT. Pour cela, vous devrez participer au mini-jeu d'Igor le fossoyeur, un brave homme, qui vous sera utile plus d'une fois au cours de l'aventure.
extrait: Découvrez comment récupérer le quart de coeur enfoui dans le cimetière du remake Switch 2 de Zelda OOT. Pour cela, vous devrez participer au mini-jeu d'Igor le fossoyeur, un brave homme, qui vous sera utile plus d'une fois au cours de l'aventure. Dans Zelda Ocarina of Time, vous aurez à compléter toutes les activités annexes du jeu pour mettre la main sur 100% des objets contenus dans vos fenêtres de personnage. Cela ne débloque rien, mais vous pourrez au moins vous dire que vous avez complété ce chef d'oeuvre à fond. Dans ce guide très rapide, on voit quelle est la tombe gagnante dans le mini-jeu d'Igor au cimetière.

titre: Chant du Soleil Zekda Ocarina of Time : Comment débloquez cette partition ?
chapo: Dans ce nouveau guide, on voit comment débloquer la partition du Chant du Soleil dans le remake Switch 2 de Zelda OOT. Allez la chercher le plus tôt possible, parce qu'elle va vous être utile tout au long de votre aventure en Hyrule.
